We're here today to speak to an application that we brought forward to amend the city's official community plan to add a new land use designation for high density mixed use as well as it's supporting objectives and policies.
This new land use designation was triggered by an applicant to facilitate a particular development proposal at 555 East Lake and 40312 Street East. Next slide, please.
The official community plan is our collective vision for Saskatoon as a prairie city and a prosperous community.
It's a legal document required by the Planning and Development Act and the direction and goals are recognized by the province as a statement of Saskatoon's long term vision.
As Saskatoon's principal citywide policy document, the OCP captures the vision for growth and development by residents city council administration.
It's intended to provide both inspiration and direction and ensure that the community's vision for Saskatoon is integrated into all aspects of our planning priority setting and development.
It trenches a number of things a number of city initiatives undertaken in recent years to provide direction for development and implementation of more detailed management plans including bylaws.
So next slide, please.
A key feature of the OCP to aid in its implementation are land use designations.

A land use designation is a category of development that describes the general uses and characteristics of land within the city to help future development take place in an orderly and rational manner.
Each designation includes a description which is general in nature and provides the types of uses, densities and intensities as well as location criteria.
These descriptions are used to determine if a proposed development is appropriate for a site.
They also help guide administration to then apply the zoning bylaw and to settle precise regulations and uses.

The long term impacts of the OCP's land use map which is up on the slide is that the land use designations may reaffirm existing development patterns or they may guide how an area's character and uses may change into the future.
Next slide, please.
So the city's development framework for high density development with a mixture of uses as it stands today is facilitate this use in our downtown and to a lesser extent in the city center.
The city center surrounds the downtown and is a transitional area from downtown's higher density development to the surrounding lower density neighborhoods.
The other locations where high density mixed use development may occur is within identified transit villages along the city's corridor growth area.
The proposed development at 555 East Lake in 40312 Street East is located outside the downtown and city center within the corridor growth area but not within an identified transit village.
The development envisions a high rise building with a mixture of uses which includes residential, commercial, office, cultural and community uses.
And as such for this proposed development to move forward the applicant proposed a new land use designation to facilitate this type of development at this location.

When we receive that the administration undertook a comprehensive review of the proposed designation to this included consideration of our existing policy, the proximity and access to amenities, the infrastructure and servicing support, as well as other possible locations where this designation may be appropriate.

It's important to note that as a new land use designation if this is adopted it would be available not just for this proposed development but for all future applications where the development and location align with the proposed land use designation.
Next slide please.
An online survey was made available to the public on the cities engage page starting January 6 and ending February 28 of this year.

There was an excellent response and we consider this an excellent response for especially for policy work of 597 members of the public responding to the survey and we're very thankful to those members that did take the time to do that survey.
We do have further detail on the engagement in the appendix of this report, but some highlights that we wanted to share from the public.
Was it 65% of the respondents were in favor of high density mixed use development outside of the downtown in the city center.

The reasons ranged for their support, but from benefits to increased density, opportunities for affordable housing, sustainable development practices proximity to transit and prioritizing in fill over sprawl.
There were concerns, of course noted, specifically impacts to existing views, shadowing, potential impact of river bank stability and access to green space.
Next slide please.
From the engagement we used that feedback to develop the criteria and the what we built out based on the applicants proposed designation.
We used that to establish the location criteria and the values to associate with this new land use designation.
So this included the potential for the uses of residential commercial office, cultural and community uses.
That the sites need to be supported by all modes of transportation and accessible to high frequency transit that they be pedestrian oriented human scaled and transit oriented.
That they're in proximity to public amenities and have access to appropriate infrastructure.
They may include horizontal or vertical mixed use high density development.
That they are within walking distance to downtown and bus traffic transit stations and that they're located within the downtown city center and our strategic in fill areas.

For these last two points, it's important to establish that the high density mixed use could locate within areas where higher density development is already permitted within the downtown city center strategic in fill areas.

This type of location or this type of development with this new land use designation may locate outside of the downtown boundary as long as it's within walking distance 400 meters to downtown and one or more bus stop at transit stations.

It acknowledges that there might be sites with unique attributes outside of the downtown that could support this type of development.
But this, with this acknowledgement and the specific criteria contained in the land use designation, we're trying to ensure that the impacts to the surrounding areas are mitigated.
